name: Tardo
body:
Tardo
CR 1/2

This pale-skinned humanoid is shrouded in a great hooded cloak of flowing green. Its skin is mottled with a patchwork of brownish spots and one hand is human-like but the other is twisted into an inhuman claw.

XP 200
NE Small fey (shapechanger)
Init +3; Senses low-light vision; Perception +4

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 14, flat-footed 12 (+3 Dex, +1 natural, +1 size)
hp 7 (2d6)
Fort +0, Ref +6, Will +2
DR 2/cold iron; SR 11

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee dagger +5 (1d4-1/19-20) or dagger +3 (1d4-1/19-20) and claw +3 (1d4-1)
Spell-like Abilities (CL 9th, concentration +10)

1/day—nightmare (DC 16)

STATISTICS

Str 8, Dex 16, Con 10, Int 10, Wis 9, Cha 13
Base Atk +1; CMB -1; CMD 12
Feats Weapon Finesse
Skills Bluff +6, Climb +4, Escape Artist +8, Knowledge (nature) +5, Perception +4, Stealth +12
Languages Common, Sylvan
SQ change shape (any Small animal or humanoid, alter self or beast shape I)

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, or gang (3-8)
Treasure standard (dagger and other treasure)

The tardo is a troublesome being with the appearance of a strange urchin. It delights in changing shape, misleading travelers, and causing nightmares. Although usually more of a pest than an immediate danger, like many otherworldly creatures, they can be perilous in anger.

It is said tardos sometimes abduct young children, turning them into tardos themselves. They will target a child younger than seven years old. The tardo will make contact with the child, sometimes in a different shape or in dreams. Ideally, no adult is aware of this initial contact. When the child is ready, the tardo enchants them and takes them away. If the child is not recovered in time, usually seven years relative to the Material Plane, they may become a tardo themselves.
